clue.text: Artist's strength originally lies in length of forearm

indicators.note: the letter lies in the measure, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cubit is an old measure, the length from elbow to fingertip

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word strength

explanation.surface: An artist's power is said to come from the reach of their arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Artist' plus 's, read as 'Artist is': the answer is the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter of the Picasso and Braque school, working in geometric planes, is such an artist.

clue.text: Explorer had time for coastal trading

parts.note: John Cabot was the Venetian explorer who sailed for England to North America
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An explorer spent a period trading along the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabotage is shipping and trade between ports of a single country along its coast.

clue.text: Sort of speculator one finds running expensive bars

parts.note: a bull is a speculator who buys expecting prices to rise
I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A market speculator finds a pricey bar open for business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' look like pubs, but they are ingots of gold or silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold or silver cast in ingots is valued by weight, so the bars are costly.

clue.text: A form of painting, but not a movement

explanation.surface: Describing a painting style that is not an art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like an art movement such as Impressionism; read literally, the words describe life held motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre picture of fruit, flowers or objects is so called; and read literally, the phrase means existence without motion.

clue.text: One who declares he will not swear

definitions.text: One who declares he will not swear

parts.words: One who declares he will not swear
parts.note: a person who objects to taking a religious oath in court makes a solemn declaration instead

explanation.surface: Someone states that they refuse to use bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear' suggests cursing, but here it means taking an oath; the person who declines that in court solemnly declares instead.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a witness who will not take an oath may make a solemn non-religious statement of truth instead.

clue.text: Oil and vinegar Continentals are putting on their soup and fish, perhaps

parts.note: the French are continental Europeans

parts.words: putting on their soup and fish, perhaps
parts.note: soup and fish is old slang for formal evening dress, so putting it on is dressing

explanation.surface: Europeans put on evening wear to eat salad, soup and fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup and fish' looks like courses at dinner, but it is slang for white-tie evening clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette, the classic salad sauce of oil and vinegar, goes by this name.

clue.text: Fix up motorway foundation

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the motorway name is read from the bottom

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crossword letters
a bed is a base layer or foundation

explanation.surface: Someone repairs the base of a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, London to Leeds, is a British motorway, its 1 read as I; 'up' turns it to IM in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something firmly in surrounding matter is to fix it in place.

clue.text: Does it help some men to forget? Yes and no

definitions.text: Does it help some men to forget? Yes and no

indicators.note: the word both is and is not there in some men to, sitting concealed within the phrase

explanation.surface: Asking whether a keepsake helps people forget, with an equivocal answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' works two ways: the souvenir is there in 'some men to' and not, and a keepsake helps men, though not to forget but to remember.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or souvenir is kept as a reminder, so it helps one not to forget.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing sailor from E Indies switches sides

indicators.note: the letters for left and right swap places with each other

parts.note: a lascar was an East Indian sailor serving on European ships

explanation.surface: An Indian seaman who changes allegiance is a worthless rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right; 'switches sides' swaps them, putting R first and L last.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a scoundrel or rogue, someone worthless.

clue.text: Surgeon (RN) abroad turns into homely philanthropist

parts.note: a surgeon is a doctor

indicators.note: the letters turn into a new order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naval surgeon working overseas becomes a charitable figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' signals rearranging RN ABROAD into BARNARDO. Thomas Barnardo founded the Barnardo's children's homes in Victorian London, hence 'homely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of a chain of orphanages was a charitable benefactor associated with homes.

clue.text: Scoop water out of the sea for American bird

indicators.note: read as 'outside of', so the word for scooping water wraps around the sea

parts.note: to bale is to scoop water out of a boat
the Timor Sea lies between Australia and Timor

explanation.surface: An instruction to bail out seawater, apparently in aid of some American bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads as 'outside of', not removal. The Baltimore oriole is a North American songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltimore oriole, an orange and black songbird of eastern North America, is often just called by the city's name.

clue.text: Member in old car has collision

indicators.note: the member is placed in the old car, one piece inside another

parts.note: bus is slang for an old car
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP in a battered vehicle is involved in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: BUS is old slang for a car, especially a battered one.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock into something is to have a collision with it.

clue.text: Form or title in verse

indicators.note: rhyming verse reorders words, so the letters are rearranged here

explanation.surface: A choice between a shape and a title in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in verse' signals rearranging OR TITLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A triolet is a poetic form of eight lines with only two rhymes.

clue.text: Rebel down under ends with a flourish

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
New Zealand, abbreviated NZ, is in the antipodes

explanation.surface: A rebel in Australasia finishes his career in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends with' is a link: the pieces CADE and NZ are followed by A. Down under usually means Australia; here it is New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a showy solo passage, a musical flourish near the end of a concerto movement.

clue.text: Information one uses would provide longer spell for these djinns

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Information one uses would provide longer spell for these djinns': GEN (information) + I (one) gives GENI, but no clue word gives the final I without 'uses' doing two jobs; the clue seems to set GENII against the longer spelling GENIES and no parse fits every word
annotationWithheld.clue: Information one uses would provide longer spell for these djinns

clue.text: Editor has embarrassed Thespian

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is blushing like a ham actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor prepares a text for publication, a formal word for someone who revises copy.

clue.text: The native quarter of Worcester or Derby?

definitions.text: The native quarter of Worcester or Derby?

parts.words: The native quarter of Worcester or Derby?
parts.note: Worcester and Derby are English cities famous for their porcelain factories, so either is a porcelain town

explanation.surface: Asking which district of an English city is home to its natives.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Worcester and Royal Crown Derby are famous English porcelain makers; a porcelain city is thus a town of china, and the answer is also an ethnic district.
explanation.definitionFit: A city district where many Chinese people live and trade is the usual term, and Worcester or Derby punningly fits as porcelain towns.

clue.text: He follows blindly and, gosh, runs over a fielder!

indicators.note: in a down clue the runs sit over, that is above, the fielder

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise like gosh
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
mid-on is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side

explanation.surface: A blind follower exclaims as he runs over a cricket fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a fielding position in cricket. The Myrmidons followed Achilles into battle without question.
explanation.definitionFit: The warriors of Achilles gave their name to anyone who carries out orders slavishly.

clue.text: Instruction from the Guardian's office

explanation.surface: Teaching drawn from the offices of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper, but it is a guardian or tutor: the word means both teaching and guardianship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from tutor: teaching given by a tutor, and the role of a legal guardian over a ward.

clue.text: Out of bed, stretched, but unable to open up

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
a rope that is stretched taut is tight

explanation.surface: Someone is awake and stretching, but cannot unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open up' looks physical after stretching, but means confiding feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tense, inhibited person cannot relax or talk freely about feelings.

clue.text: Suggest I am to travel regularly

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
ferries ply a route, travelling it regularly

explanation.surface: Someone hints that they commute.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without stating it outright is to suggest it.

clue.text: Charge for peg or tee almost smashed

indicators.note: something smashed is broken up, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word tee loses its final letter

parts.note: a golf tee, taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer's peg or tee is nearly broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TEE to TE; 'smashed' rearranges PEG OR TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward or dependant under someone's care is their charge.

clue.text: About the right reading desk for a word game

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
an ambo is a raised reading desk or pulpit in early churches

explanation.surface: A lectern used for a parlour word game.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBO is an old church lectern.
explanation.definitionFit: Crambo is a game where one player gives a word and others find rhymes for it.

clue.text: Negotiated net rate for coarse cloth

indicators.note: terms that have been negotiated are worked over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A trader agrees a net price for some rough fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiated' signals rearranging NET RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratteen is an old name for a thick twilled woollen fabric.

clue.text: Bird dog with black head

indicators.note: head points to the leading letter of the dog's name, which is taken away

parts.note: a beagle is a hunting dog
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gun dog with a dark head.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'dog with black head' as the dog's name is the bird's with B (black) at its head; take B off BEAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Cabin, perhaps, where there is space to move about

explanation.surface: A ship's cabin offers room to walk around.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is literal, a room at sea such as a cabin; the other is the open water a ship needs to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a room on a ship; and sailors use the term for open water clear enough for a vessel to steer safely.

clue.text: Guildhall porter's comic turn rejected

parts.note: a comic is a kind of magazine, or mag

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: your turn in a game is your go

explanation.surface: A doorman at the Guildhall has his comedy routine turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic turn' looks like a stand-up act. Gog and Magog are the giant figures that guard London's Guildhall, so the porter's is read as 'porter is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gog and Magog are the legendary giants whose carved figures stand guard in London's Guildhall, its symbolic doorkeepers.

clue.text: Become exhausted in hurry to visit daughter

parts.note: to hurry is to run
taken as written
to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: Someone wears themselves out rushing to call on their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that bolts goes to flower and seed and declines, hence an idiom for a person or place going downhill.

clue.text: What Hamlet's players were not to do to the King of Judaea

definitions.text: What Hamlet's players were not to do to the King of Judaea

parts.words: What Hamlet's players were not to do to the King of Judaea
parts.note: Hamlet warns the visiting actors against ranting more than the tyrant king of the mystery plays

explanation.surface: A question about Hamlet's advice to the touring actors.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet III.ii the prince says an overacting player 'out-Herods Herod': Herod, King of Judaea, was the ranting villain of medieval mystery plays.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo the bombastic stage tyrant in ranting is to overact wildly.

clue.text: US student teacher to detain in the country

explanation.surface: An American trainee teacher is held within the nation's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue has a stray '29' at the start; the printed page does not.
explanation.definitionFit: In America a trainee teacher or doctor is so called; and governments in wartime confine enemy aliens within the country.
